newsitem.title: USA: Mexico's Zedillo says '96 GDP growth to be 4.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo says '96 GDP growth to be 4.0 pct.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo said his country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth will exceed 4.0 percent in 1996, well above previous government expectations for a 3.0 percent gain.

"And so today, our economy has moved well into recovery...GDP growth will exceed four percent for the year, considerably higher than the three percent we had anticipated," he said. His comments were made available prior to a speech he was scheduled to give to financiers and the press in New York.
Looking ahead, Zedillo estimated GDP would grow at least 4.0 percent in 1997.
He said Mexico would strive for sustained GDP growth between 5.0 and 6.0 percent in 1998 and beyond.

"We are aiming for (1997) GDP growth of at least four percent and a further reduction of inflation," he said, adding growth will be propelled by a sustained expansion in exports, a significant increase in investment, and a gradual recovery of domestic consumption.
"My commitment to strict fiscal and monetary discipline is unshakeable," he said.
Zedillo called the current maturity profile of Mexico's external debt "quite manageable" and estimated a $6.0 billion 1996 trade surplus, compared to a $7.1 billion surplus in 1995.
He also estimated new investment of as much as $2.2 billion in the telecommunications industry in 1997.
Zedillo also said that Mexico has taken major steps to improve its domestic savings rate, which he said has been a source of concern since the early 1970's.
Regarding corruption, Zedillo said he has reinforced the judicial system, improved law enforcement and led the fight against corruption, drug trafficking and organized crime.
"I've said, and our actions have demonstrated, that no one -- absolutely no one -- in Mexico today is above the law," he said.
